inputBoundary: One caller-supplied finite Wi-Fi received-signal-strength value expressed in dBm from the study trace. Technology selection, Android field decoding, trace joins, measurement calibration, and missing/censored-value handling occur upstream.
outputBoundary: For this canonical trace-analysis variant only, classify Wi-Fi RSSI below or equal to -80 dBm as poor and values above -80 dBm as not_poor.
limitations: The first definition says '-80 dBm and below' while nearby trace prose paraphrases poor signal as 'below -80 dBm'; this binding implements only the canonical <= trace-analysis atom and does not adjudicate or erase that wording conflict.
The paper's controlled validation separately uses RSSI < -80 dBm in method-setting-9897b5f9ba40756397553301; that strict validation variant is not substituted for this trace-analysis setting.
The source does not disclose a measurement serialization type, quantization rule, physical range, rounding, or tolerance, so none is invented around -80 dBm.
A missing or nonfinite RSSI value fails closed before classification.

This binding does not parse collector records, select Wi-Fi rows, reconstruct byte-counter deltas, infer screen state, calculate time or traffic fractions, aggregate participants, or reproduce the 3,785-user trace.

Controlled packet/power experiments, the eprof model, trained artifacts, validation figures, and what-if analyses are outside this threshold boundary and remain blocked without their source-qualified inputs and runtime.
